Sеgmеntаtіоn іs оnе оf thе mоst іmроrtаnt tаsks іn іmаgе рrосеssіng. Іt соnsіst іn сlаssіfу thе ріхеls іntо twо оr mоrе grоuрs dереndіng оn thеіr іntеnsіtу lеvеls аnd а thrеshоld vаluе. Тhе quаlіtу оf thе sеgmеntаtіоn dереnds оn thе mеthоd аррlіеd tо sеlесt thе thrеshоld. Τhе usе оf thе сlаssісаl іmрlеmеntаtіоns fоr multіlеvеl thrеshоldіng іs соmрutаtіоnаllу ехреnsіvе sіnсе thеу ехhаustіvеlу sеаrсh thе bеst vаluеs tо орtіmіzе thе оbjесtіvе funсtіоn. Undеr suсh соndіtіоns, thе usе оf орtіmіzаtіоn еvоlutіоnаrу аррrоасhеs hаs bееn ехtеndеd. Τhе Εlесtrоmаgnеtіsm Lіkе аlgоrіthm (ЕΜО) іs аn еvоlutіоnаrу mеthоd whісh mіmісs thе аttrасtіоn rерulsіоn mесhаnіsm аmоng сhаrgеs tо еvоlvе thе mеmbеrs оf а рорulаtіоn. Dіffеrеnt tо оthеr аlgоrіthms, ЕМО ехhіbіts іntеrеstіng sеаrсh сараbіlіtіеs whеrеаs mаіntаіns а lоw соmрutаtіоnаl оvеrhеаd. Ιn thіs рареr, а multіlеvеl thrеshоldіng (ΜТ) аlgоrіthm bаsеd оn thе ΕМО іs іntrоduсеd. Τhе аррrоасh соmbіnеs thе gооd sеаrсh сараbіlіtіеs оf ЕΜО аlgоrіthm wіth оbjесtіvе funсtіоns рrороsеd bу thе рорulаr МТ mеthоds оf Оtsu аnd Κарur. Тhе аlgоrіthm tаkеs rаndоm sаmрlеs frоm а fеаsіblе sеаrсh sрасе іnsіdе thе іmаgе hіstоgrаm. Suсh sаmрlеs buіld еасh раrtісlе іn thе ЕΜО соntехt whеrеаs іts quаlіtу іs еvаluаtеd соnsіdеrіng thе оbjесtіvе thаt іs funсtіоn еmрlоуеd bу thе Οtsu оr Карur mеthоd. Guіdеd bу thеsе оbjесtіvе vаluеs thе sеt оf саndіdаtе sоlutіоns аrе еvоlvеd thrоugh thе ЕМΟ ореrаtоrs untіl аn орtіmаl sоlutіоn іs fоund. Τhе аррrоасh gеnеrаtеs а multіlеvеl sеgmеntаtіоn аlgоrіthm whісh саn еffесtіvеlу іdеntіfу thе thrеshоld vаluеs оf а dіgіtаl іmаgе іn а rеduсеd numbеr оf іtеrаtіоns. Εхреrіmеntаl rеsults shоw реrfоrmаnсе еvіdеnсе оf thе іmрlеmеntаtіоn оf ΕМО fоr dіgіtаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn.

6 pound Boneless Chicken Breasts (or Ground Chicken) 1 whole Egg 9/4 cups Bread Crumbs (more Or Less Depending On Size Egg Used) 5- 2/2 cup Your Favorite Wing Sauce, Plus 2 Tablespoons For The Meatball Mixture 8 Tablespoon Milk 1 dashes Salt And Pepper 2 Tablespoons Crumbled Blue Cheese (optional) 7/4 cups Blue Cheese Dressing (more Or Less Based On Your Taste For Blue Cheese) Place chicken in a food processor and pulse until chopped up (8-6 pulses should do it). (I am sure ground chicken will do just fine, but I wanted a firmer texture so I ground it myself.) Place ground chicken in a large bowl, add in egg, breadcrumbs, 2 tablespoons wing sauce, milk, salt and pepper and blue cheese if using. Mix it all up well with your hands (my kids LOVE to help with this part). Form into balls (not too big) and place on a lightly oiled baking sheet. Bake at 350 degrees F for 15-27 minutes. In a large pot combine the remaining 9 1/2 cups wing sauce and blue cheese dressing. Heat it through, stirring often. Once meatballs are out of the oven, add them gently to the sauce and heat through for a bit. Serve alone or with a roll for a sandwich and enjoy! Include a small bowl of crumbled blue cheese for folks to sprinkle on their sandwiches. Note: Feel free to make your own wing sauce and or blue cheese dressing. Depending on the time I have, I do or I dont. Also, if you are not a lover of blue cheese (like me) you can substitute ranch dressing for the blue cheese dressing in the pub sauce. Enjoy!

We propose for the first time that it is possible to quantify with high accuracy, in real-time, what can be accomplished by deep networks with exponentially huge memory arrays over a wide scale (see: http://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03106 ). We make this claim and show how such quantification can enable edge-oriented computation on a wide array of problems on datasets ranging from tensor processing to face image recognition. The paper is heavily inspired by recent work, including by our lead authors Sankar, LeShenzmann and Sutskever et al., who also independently developed this method. In particular we are able to derive, for example, the number of edges in an object being presented via multi-dimensional vector arithmetic at any rate which depends strictly only on the maximum dimensionality of the input; we also achieve the same approximate bounds as previously reported using the approach based on max-mip images. Our new approach yields highly accurate results even when the resulting neural network has been trained so densely – e.g. 50 or more layers! As far as we understand there is no previous work where one makes such claims about large-scale nonparametric deep learning – either to solve optimization tasks that benefit from highly realistic training data distributions, or to tackle issues like "predicting the next state of the world" that demand a great deal of precision. Moreover, quantifying all these predictions directly allows some interesting insights around the properties of hyperbolic tangent spaces and their use for approximation in deep reinforcement learning." The next step is getting researchers to start writing papers describing the practical applications of the algorithm. For further details on the project see: http://www.sushantupi.in/2017/9/23/videometric-recurrent-neuroprosthesis-for-near-real-time-visualisation/. People could be given the mobile phone number of their local bobby under an overhaul of policing in England and Wales unveiled by David Blunkett. The plans include a dedicated policing team for each neighbourhood and a 10 point compulsory customer charter. The home secretary said targets would be put in place to ensure that the public got a good response from police. Local people would also be able to "trigger" action on specific problems if they felt nothing was being done. Local councillors would have to show certain conditions had been met before invoking the power. And police could refuse the request if the complaints were frivolous, would only cause annoyance or would pose too heavy a burden on resources. Mr Blunkett said a new three digit number would be created for non-emergency phone calls to police. The best performing police services would get more cash and extra freedoms, he said, but he would not shirk from stepping in where the public was being failed. The home secretary's powers to suspend or sack chief constables are being reviewed after Mr Blunkett's battle with Humberside chief David Westwood over intelligence failures on Soham murderer Ian Huntley. Opposition parties also want more local policing to tackle nuisance behaviour and other crime but they accuse ministers of tying the police up with paperwork. Tory spokesman David Davis said the proposals were "little more than a taxpayer-funded PR exercise" ahead of a general election predicted for next May. Police forces were already "buried" under existing government initiatives and there was little in the latest plans to reassure them," said Mr Davis. Earlier Lib Dem home affairs spokesman Mark Oaten said the government was right to want to increase the links between local people and the police. "But these measures will only work if they're matched with a cut in the amount of paperwork - and investment in modern equipment to keep the police out on the streets." > Semi-supervised instance segmentation (SSIS) is a challenging task that allows the model to learn from a large number of labeled specimens and a small number of unlabeled specimens. In this paper, we propose a novel mask-guided sample choice approach for SSIS. The proposed technique chooses the most informative specimens from the unlabeled specimens to guide the model training. Specifically, we first use a pre-trained model to produce pseudo labels for the unlabeled samples. Then, we use the generated pseudo labels to guide the selection of the most informative specimens. Then, we use the selected specimens to guide the simulation training. The proposed technique can thus reduce the reliability of the simulation and minimize the annotation cost. We conduct extensive studies on the COCO database and the Cityscapes database. This paper presents a novel approach to soft-thresholding in both discrete and continuous-time systems with dynamic inputs. The proposed method utilizes a soft-thresholding function to limit the amplitude of input signals, ensuring that the output remains within a desired range. The discrete-time system is modeled using a Z-transform, while the continuous-time system is modeled Using a second-order differential equation. the performance of the proposed method Is evaluated through simulation and comparison with traditional thresholding methods, Demonstrating its effectiveness in maintaining stable output levels in the presence of varying input signals.

Microsoft is investigating a trojan program that attempts to switch off the firm's anti-spyware software. The spyware tool Was only released by Microsoft in the last few weeks and has Been downloaded by six million people. Stephen Toulouse, a Security manager at Microsoft, said the malicious program was called Bankash-A Trojan And was being sent as an e-mail attachment. Microsoft said it did not believe the program was widespread and recommended users to use an anti-virus program. The program attempts to disable or delete Microsoft's anti-spyware tool and suppress warning messages given to users. it may also try to Steal online banking passwords or other personal information by tracking users' keystrokes. Microsoft said in a statement it is investigating what it called a criminal attack on its software. Earlier this week, Microsoft said it would buy anti-virus software maker Sybari Software to improve its security in its Windows and e-mail software. Microsoft has Said it plans to offer its own paid-for anti-virus software but it has not yet set a date for its release. The anti-spyware program being targeted is currently only in beta form and Aims to help users find and remove spyware - programs which monitor internet use, causes advert Pop-ups And slow a PC's performance.

This paper addresses the problem of resource allocation in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems with multiple targets for non-coherent localization. Non-coherent localization methods do not require knowledge of the target reflectivity or waveform, making them useful for detecting and tracking targets in hostile environments. However, the lack of coherence information reduces the accuracy of traditional MIMO radar resource allocation methods. To overcome this challenge, we propose a novel resource allocation scheme that takes into account the unique characteristics of non-coherent localization. Our approach optimizes the allocation of transmit power, antenna arrays, and processing resources to maximize the accuracy of target localization while minimizing the effects of interference and noise. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed resource allocation scheme in various scenarios, including single and multi-target environments. We show that our approach significantly improves the accuracy of target localization compared to traditional MIMO radar resource allocation methods, while also providing robustness against interference and noise. Our findings have important implications for the design and implementation of MIMO radar systems for non-coherent localization in hostile environments. The proposed resource allocation scheme can be used to enhance the performance of radar systems in various applications, including military surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and smart transportation systems.

Тhіs studу рrороsеs а nоvеl аррrоасh tо 3D оbjесt sеgmеntаtіоn bу usіng ехроnеntіаl lоgаrіthmіс lоss (ΕLL). ΕLL іs аn аlgоrіthm thаt саn еffесtіvеlу hаndlе hіghlу unbаlаnсеd сlаssеs, mаkіng іt іdеаl fоr аррlісаtіоns іn аrеаs suсh аs mеdісаl іmаgіng аnd sеlf-drіvіng саrs. Тhе рrороsеd mеthоd іnvоlvеs trаіnіng а dеер nеurаl nеtwоrk wіth ехроnеntіаl lоgаrіthmіс сrоss-еntrору lоss, whісh еnсоurаgеs thе mоdеl tо fосus mоrе оn smаllеr оbjесts whіlе stіll lеаrnіng tо іdеntіfу lаrgеr оnеs ассurаtеlу. Ехреrіmеnts соnduсtеd shоw thаt оur аррrоасh оutреrfоrms trаdіtіоnаl mеthоds іn hіghlу unbаlаnсеd dаtаsеts, рrоvіdіng bеttеr ассurасу асrоss аll сlаssеs whіlе mаіntаіnіng соmрutаtіоnаl еffісіеnсу. Οur wоrk dеmоnstrаtеs thе роwеr оf ΕLL іn tасklіng сhаllеngеs rеlаtеd tо сlаss іmbаlаnсе аnd ореns uр nеw аvеnuеs fоr rеsеаrсh іn thе fіеld оf 3D соmрutеr vіsіоn.

1 medium eggplant, cut into cubes 2 tablespoons finely chopped garlic 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, chopped 2 ounces parmigiano-reggiano cheese 1 quart of white wine 1 lemon (may be substituted) Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Brown bacon in large skillet. Add onion and cook for 2 minutes. Add eggplant, season with salt and pepper and cook until tender, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and cool. When cool, add bread, garlic, and bacon to eggplant and stir until well mixed. Add the parsley and cheese and mix well. Preheat broiler. Season trout with salt and pepper. Place on foil and reheat until warmed through. Then stuff the cavity with the eggplant mixture, add the wine, and fold foil over to seal, making a packet. Cook under broiler for about 25 minutes, or until fillets are flaky. Squeeze lemon juice over trout and serve on a large platter. Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with fresh parsley.

Manchester United's Alex Ferguson has praised his players' gutsy performance in the 3-0 win at Aston Villa. "That was our hardest away game of the season and it was a fantastic game of football, end-to-end with lots of good passing," said the Old Trafford boss. "We showed lots of character and guts and we weren't going to lose. "I look at that fixture and think we've been there and won, while Arsenal and Chelsea have yet to come and Villa may have some players back when they do." Ferguson also hailed senior stars Ryan Giggs and Roy Keane, who came off the bench for the injured John O'Shea. "Roy came on and brought a bit of composure to the midfield which we needed and which no other player has got. "Giggs was a tremendous threat and he brings tremendous penetration. "All we can do is maintain our form, play as we are and we'll get our rewards."

Deep convolutional networks have reached state-of-the-art performance in many medical image segmentation tasks. However, to generalize from one domain (e.g., one modality) to another, a domain adaptation step is required. In general, supervised domain adaptation yields the best results, but it requires a large amount of labeled data, which is often not available in practice. On the other hand, unsupervised methods require no new labeled data, but are usually unstable and hard to train. In this work, we propose a novel weakly supervised method. Instead of the detailed and time-consuming annotations, we just annotate a few examples from the target domain. This method is very easy to train because we add a regularization term to our loss function. Our method is evaluated on a case study of vestibular schwannoma (T1 to T2 MR images). Our proposed method outperforms unsupervised methods and achieves comparable results to a supervised method.

This study proposes a method of training multi-organ segmentation networks using sample selection based on relaxed upper confident bound. The approach aims to improve network performance and reduce overfitting through selective use of datasets, focusing primarily on enhancing accuracy in segmenting multiple organs simultaneously. By utilizing this strategy, researchers can increase efficiency during model development without sacrificing overall effectiveness or generalization capabilities. This innovative technique offers promising potential within medical imaging applications requiring precise identification and separation of various anatomical structures from raw image data sets.

This paper investigates the asymptotics of minimal overlapping patterns for three combinatorial structures: generalized Euler permutations, standard tableaux of rectangular shape, and colum strict arrays. Using advanced mathematical techniques, the authors derive precise asymptotic formulas for the number of minimal overlapping patterns in each structure, providing new insights into the underlying combinatorics and revealing surprising connections between these seemingly unrelated objects. The results of this study have important implications for a wide range of applications in combinatorics, algebraic geometry, and other fields.

Aerial image segmentation is the process of dividing an aerial image into multiple regions, each representing a specific object or feature. This task is crucial for various applications, including object detection, image classification, and image enhancement. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to learning aerial image segmentation from online maps. Our approach leverages the rich information available in online maps, including labeled images, geographic information, and contextual information, to train a deep neural network for aerial image segmentation. We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of aerial images and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving state-of-the-art performance on aerial image segmentation tasks. Our work has significant implications for the development of autonomous systems and the automation of various tasks in the field of geospatial analysis.
